They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions. 8→ 9→## How it works 10→ 11→React extends the HTML [`
`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [`action`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute. 12→ 13→When used in a form, the function automatically receives the [`FormData`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [`FormData` methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods): 14→ 15→```tsx filename="app/invoices/page.tsx" switcher 16→export default function Page() { 17→ async function createInvoice(formData: FormData) { 18→ 'use server' 19→ 20→ const rawFormData = { 21→ customerId: formData.get('customerId'), 22→ amount: formData.get('amount'), 23→ status: formData.get('status'), 24→ } 25→ 26→ // mutate data 27→ // revalidate the cache 28→ } 29→ 30→ return ...

...

For example: `const rawFormData = Object.fromEntries(formData)`. Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with `$ACTION_`. 54→ 55→## Passing additional arguments 56→ 57→Outside of form fields, you can pass additional arguments to a Server Function using the JavaScript [`bind`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind) method. However, the value will be part of the rendered HTML and will not be encoded. 110→> - `bind` works in both Server and Client Components and supports progressive enhancement. 111→ 112→## Form validation 113→ 114→Forms can be validated on the client or server. 115→ 116→- For **client-side validation**, you can use the HTML attributes like `required` and `type="email"` for basic validation. 117→- For **server-side validation**, you can use a library like [zod](https://zod.dev/) to validate the form fields.
